why_it_is_a_useful_negative_control: Long-lived formal subtypes were eventually removed because of poor stability, reliability, validity, longitudinal distinction and treatment-response specificity. Tests classification inertia and administrative persistence.

A biologically attractive subdivision was proposed with etiologic, prognostic and treatment promises, but renin classification varied markedly with diet, posture and analytic approach and promised prognostic/therapeutic utility did not hold consistently. Tests biomarker-defined splits that are mechanistically plausible but measurement-sensitive.
key_sources: Holle et al Arch Intern Med 1978; Kaplan JAMA 1977 doi:10.1001/jama.1977.03280070051023; Thurston & Swales Lancet 1976

why_it_is_a_useful_negative_control: Historically influential binary phenotype, but categories overlapped and could not adequately distinguish many patients; later systems-biology and mechanistic endotypes superseded the simple dichotomy. Useful within-disease example of a weak split being replaced by a more coherent one.
key_sources: Lee et al PMC6411459; childhood asthma phenotype reviews

why_it_is_a_useful_negative_control: Consensus definitions were repeatedly revised; Sepsis-3 abandoned SIRS as the defining framework and eliminated severe sepsis. Useful operational-category control because classification was driven by clinical identification/prognosis and consensus rather than proof of separate diseases.
